correctness.rationale: The full deck reduces exactly to the unordered two inward Parikh paths through depth \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), plus total composition and (for odd n) the forced center. Two distinct vertices at consecutive levels admit at most one unit-increment perfect matching; if both cross and straight existed, equality of two nonzero differences of unit vectors would force the supposedly distinct next vertices equal. For \(n\le5\) no internal two-excursion switch survives modulo reversal. For \(n=6\) precisely separated levels 1 and 3 joined by equal level 2 admit two reversal orbits; these are exactly \(abcdab, abdcab, bacdba, badcba\) with \(a\ne b\) and \(c\ne d\). The unordered pairs at length one and length three are recoverable uniquely, yielding \(\binom q2^2\) fibers. Palindromes contribute \(q^3\) singleton fibers, and all other nonexceptional words pair with their reversals. This proves the exact size distribution and class count for every \(q\ge2\); the exhaustive independent checks \(2\le q\le7\), \(1\le n\le6\) corroborate but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The binary first collision and short-length uniqueness are credited to Ye–Elishco, Example III.6 and Corollary III.12 (arxiv:2208.14963). The claim is the all-alphabet structural classification of every length-six fiber, its indexed four-word families of support up to four, exact distribution, and q-uniform optimal zero-error code size. Full-text comparisons of two foundational binary sources and a later binary error-coding treatment, relevant semantic publication searches, and the inspected published statements did not reveal a dominating q-ary result. Lack of indexed coverage is not conclusive; alternate terminology is an acknowledged risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed all-alphabet version of the six-position classification or a logically stronger unpublished theorem may exist.
Further related full texts outside the inspected sources could contain an equivalent finite case study.

value.rationale: The theorem settles a natural sharp onset problem across every finite alphabet, determines every exceptional fiber rather than just exhibiting a collision, and computes exact zero-error reconstruction capacity. The \(q=4\) full-support collision shows new multi-symbol behavior beyond the published binary case. The invariant is the complete observation fiber distribution at the first ambiguous length, not an arbitrary coordinate slice or a routine recomputation of a known table.
